title: v3 Phase 1: intelligent lens routing + workflow review wave
summary: Replace filename-glob-only lens routing with a deterministic per-lens applicability engine (content + graph + requirement signals, verdict deep|light|n/a-with-negative-evidence, budget 5-7 deep / hard cap 8, security and architecture floors), stage lens profiles as catalog data, an honest coverage map + HEADLINE, and a detector-fixture + full-catalog-audit discipline that auto-files router regressions. Ship the review wave as a Claude plugin workflow (workflows/review-wave.js) consuming the same dispatch briefs, with capability detection and a MANDATORY byte-identical fallback to today's Task-based dispatch (Codex has no workflow runtime).
decision: Adopt a detector-per-lens applicability engine in a new stdlib-only module taskplane/lens_signals.py, wired into lens.route() as an opt-in v2 path gated on stage_profiles catalog data (legacy path byte-identical when absent); render routing honesty in dashboard coverage map + HEADLINE; formalize the brief handoff as contract:lens-brief and the findings shape as contract:findings-v2 so the workflow path (workflows/review-wave.js) and the Task-dispatch path consume identical briefs and produce byte-equivalent artifacts, with capability detection, path tracing, and a CI Codex parity guard.

current_state.summary: lens.route() selects deep lenses from file globs, task type, artifact type, a code baseline flag, and the graph hub score only (taskplane/lens.py:164-274); hub signal and its fail-toward-more-coverage behavior at taskplane/lens.py:108-137; architecture floor (never skip on code) at taskplane/lens.py:216-219; breadth='all' sweeps every non-routed lens (taskplane/lens.py:248-261) and is mandated at the em step (taskplane/loop.py:853-856); dispatch briefs with per-task TASKPLANE_TASK slots and read-only contracts are built in lens.dispatch_briefs (taskplane/lens.py:405-480), slot activation at taskplane/lens.py:374-385, findings shape prose-pinned at taskplane/lens.py:397-401; the catalog holds 26 lenses with globs/task_types/baseline and no stage or content awareness (lenses/catalog.json); the dashboard renders coverage only as deep/sweep/did-not-fire (taskplane/dashboard.py:1076-1128) with the HEADLINE segment at taskplane/dashboard.py:201 and 804-806; depgraph nodes are directory-level modules plus boundary nodes prefixed contract:/resource:/svc:/ext: (taskplane/depgraph.py:222-274) — no lens-relevance data on nodes. Claude hosts ship Dynamic Workflows (schema-validated agent(), journaled, resumable); Codex has NO workflow runtime, so Task dispatch is the Codex path (docs/v3-strategy-flows-lenses-onboarding.md, addendum). Measured dogfood: ~1.3-1.5M tokens per breadth=all review.

alternatives.name: Detector-per-lens applicability engine (deterministic, stdlib-only)
alternatives.description: Per lens, a cheap deterministic detector computes {score, evidence[], negative_evidence[]} from content (bounded text scans: i18n, UI markup, SQL, HTTP/queue clients, auth/PII, concurrency, platform APIs), graph (component kind, hub score, boundary contracts), and requirement (acceptance-criteria keywords) signals; the router maps scores to deep|light|n/a-with-negative-evidence within the active stage profile, under a 5-7 deep budget (hard cap 8, overflow demoted to light) and security/architecture floors.

gains: Deterministic and explainable: same inputs always produce the same routing, every verdict carries machine-checkable evidence
50-70% projected token reduction per review with higher precision (fewer observation-class findings from irrelevant lenses)
Honesty is enforceable: n/a requires negative evidence, the coverage map shows every disposition, the audit sweep auto-files misses as router regressions
Zero new dependencies (stdlib re/os/json), testable with plain positive/negative fixtures
costs: 26 detectors to author and maintain; detector false negatives become a new regression surface (mitigated by mandatory fixtures + the audit backstop)
Bounded content scanning adds I/O per route (capped at 64KB/file, 200 files, <1s per component, perf-tested)
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Detector maintenance cost exceeds the measured token savings, or the audit loop sustains repeated escapes (>0 per release) indicating the deterministic signal model cannot keep up with the codebase

alternatives.name: LLM-classifier routing per review
alternatives.description: Ask a cheap model at review time which lenses apply to the diff and route on its answer.

gains: Adapts to novel content without writing new detectors
costs: Nondeterministic: the same diff can route differently across runs, breaking fixture tests, the audit loop's ground truth, and coverage-map verifiability
Costs tokens to save tokens: a classifier pass on every review
Negative evidence would be model prose, not machine-checkable — violates the standing rule that skipping a lens is only legal with machine-checkable negative evidence
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A host ships a free, deterministic, reproducible classification primitive whose outputs can be pinned in fixtures

alternatives.name: Static per-directory lens config
alternatives.description: A checked-in map from directories/globs to lens sets (e.g. lens-map.yaml) that the router reads instead of computing applicability.

gains: Trivially deterministic and near-zero runtime cost
costs: Rots: the map encodes yesterday's contents and nothing invalidates it when code changes (a directory that gains SQL keeps its stale lens set)
No evidence: an n/a is a config line, not a checkable claim about the code, so the no-silent-skip rule cannot be enforced
Per-repo authoring burden pushes users to over-broad maps (back to sweeping) or under-broad maps (silent narrowing — the killer risk)
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Operators need a pinning/override layer ON TOP of detectors; never as the primary mechanism

contracts.description: New stage_profiles data block in lenses/catalog.json mapping stage (design/build/review) to the candidate lens-id set; the router is restricted to the active stage's profile; adding a lens to a profile is a data change with no code change; a drift test pins every profile id to a real catalog lens id.

The dispatch-brief payload emitted by lens.dispatch_briefs (id, name, tier, agent, model_tier, task_slot, output, read-only contract spec, verbatim prompt) extended additively with the routing verdict, score, and evidence. It is the single handoff consumed by BOTH the workflow path (workflows/review-wave.js via args) and the Task-dispatch path (Codex), which is what makes the two paths byte-equivalent by construction.

Schema-pinned findings.json shape per lens agent: lens id + findings[{severity, class, file, line, title, scenario, fix}] plus meta.lens_coverage carrying the full routing decision {lens: {verdict, score, evidence|negative_evidence}}. Enforced as the agent() output schema on the workflow path (retry-on-mismatch) and validated at merge on both paths; dashboard renders both the v2 and legacy coverage shapes.

acceptance_map.criterion: Stage lens profiles exist as catalog data and the router is restricted to the active stage's profile (design-stage route never selects code-quality)
acceptance_map.design_element: stage_profiles data block in lenses/catalog.json (contract:stage-profiles) + route v2 stage parameter restricting the candidate set
acceptance_map.validation: Unit test: a design-stage route over a code diff never yields code-quality; test with a modified catalog proves adding a lens to a profile changes routing with zero code change; catalog drift test pins profile ids to real lens ids

acceptance_map.criterion: Every lens in the active profile gets a deterministic applicability verdict deep|light|n/a computed from content+graph+requirement signals in under 1s per component
acceptance_map.design_element: taskplane/lens_signals.py detector registry (one detector or always/inherit marker per catalog lens) with bounded content scans (64KB/file, 200 files, stdlib re, sorted iteration), graph signals via hub_signal/boundary nodes, requirement keyword signals; verdict thresholds deep>=0.6, light>=0.2
acceptance_map.validation: Registry-vs-catalog drift test; determinism test (two identical runs produce byte-identical routing); perf test asserting <1s per component on the largest fixture; per-detector fixture tests

acceptance_map.criterion: An n/a verdict always carries machine-checkable negative evidence (e.g. '0 i18n signals: no locale files, no i18n imports, no user-facing string literals')
acceptance_map.design_element: Signal.negative_evidence is required whenever score==0; the router refuses to emit an n/a verdict without it (raises, falling back to light)
acceptance_map.validation: Unit test: constructing an n/a routing entry without negative evidence is rejected; the i18n detector on taskPlane's own repo yields n/a with the exact negative-evidence string (negative fixture)

acceptance_map.criterion: Deep set is capped at 8 (ranked by score, overflow demoted to light, never dropped) with floors: security cannot be n/a on enforcement/boundary-touching diffs; architecture is at least light on any code change
acceptance_map.design_element: Budget ranker in lens_signals (target 5-7 deep, hard cap 8, overflow demoted to light) with floor rules applied post-ranking: security floor triggered by enforcement/boundary surfaces (hooks/**, auth globs, contract-screen code, boundary-contract edges in impact); architecture floor preserves taskplane/lens.py:216-219 semantics
acceptance_map.validation: Test: a max-signal fixture yields exactly 8 deep with every remaining profile lens light or n/a (none absent); test: an enforcement-touching diff can never route security to n/a even with a zero content score; test: any code diff keeps architecture >= light; forced-lens test runs a lens despite n/a

acceptance_map.criterion: Coverage map and HEADLINE show all 26 lenses as deep/light/n-a-with-reason; findings meta carries the full routing decision with evidence; --lens forces any lens; --breadth all still available
acceptance_map.design_element: Coverage-map v2 shape {lens: {verdict, score, evidence|negative_evidence}} in findings meta.lens_coverage; dashboard.lens_coverage/render_lens_coverage accept both v2 and legacy shapes and render a reason on every n/a chip; new pinned HEADLINE segment 'lenses N deep · N light · N n/a (evidenced) of 26'; --lens force recorded as 'deep (forced)'; breadth=all sweep path untouched
acceptance_map.validation: Render test: coverage map lists a reason string for every n/a lens and all 26 chips appear; HEADLINE format pinned by test; legacy-shape metas still render (compat test); --lens force test; existing breadth=all tests pass unchanged

acceptance_map.criterion: Every detector has at least one positive and one negative fixture test; a full-catalog audit run diffs findings against the routing decision and auto-files any finding from an n/a lens as a router regression
acceptance_map.design_element: taskplane/tests/fixtures/detectors/<lens>/{positive,negative} fixture pairs enforced by a CI completeness test; audit sweep (every Nth review, default 5, or release review) runs breadth=all and diffs merged findings against the routing decision, auto-filing findings from n/a-routed lenses as class:regression owner:router
acceptance_map.validation: CI test asserts every detector registry id has both fixture directories with at least one case each; audit test with a deliberately-broken detector on a fixture repo auto-files the router-regression finding with class regression and owner router

risks.risk: Silent narrowing: a detector false negative routes a relevant lens to n/a and real findings are missed (the killer risk)
risks.mitigation: Three independent guards: n/a requires machine-generated negative evidence (evidence-less n/a is rejected in code); the coverage map + HEADLINE render every disposition so a human sees each skip; the periodic full-catalog audit sweep diffs findings vs routing and auto-files any n/a-lens finding as a class:regression owned by router

risks.risk: Codex/dispatch path drifts as workflow support lands, breaking byte-identity
risks.mitigation: Both paths consume one contract:lens-brief payload with verbatim prompts; the CI Codex parity leg replays frozen briefs through the dispatch path against goldens and fails independently of workflow-path tests

risks.risk: Detector content scans blow the <1s budget or behave nondeterministically on large diffs
risks.mitigation: Hard bounds (64KB/file, 200 files, stdlib re, sorted iteration, no time/random), a perf test on the largest fixture, and a determinism test comparing two identical runs byte-for-byte

risks.risk: Stage profiles mis-scoped (a lens missing from a profile can never route in that stage)
risks.mitigation: Profiles are data (one-line change to fix); the review profile is the FULL catalog so final reviews can never be profile-narrowed; unknown stage falls open to the full catalog; catalog drift test pins profile ids

risks.risk: Applicability engine itself fails at runtime (bug, malformed catalog) and quietly shrinks review coverage
risks.mitigation: Fail toward MORE coverage, mirroring hub_signal (taskplane/lens.py:121-137): any engine exception falls back to breadth=all, warns on stderr, and traces the failure; a fail-open test pins this behavior

failure_modes.mode: Detector engine raises or returns malformed signals during routing
failure_modes.detection: Exception caught at the route v2 boundary; stderr warning + lens_engine_failed trace event
failure_modes.recovery: Automatic fallback to breadth=all for that review (more coverage, never less); the trace surfaces the failure for repair; no state is corrupted

failure_modes.mode: Workflow run dies mid-wave (credit cutoff, host kill)
failure_modes.detection: Workflow journal shows incomplete agents; missing .em-review/lens-<id>/findings.json for unfinished lenses
failure_modes.recovery: Resume the journaled run — completed agents return cached results; on hosts without workflows this failure class is unchanged from today (re-dispatch the missing briefs); leaked contracts are released via the existing orphan auto-release backstop

failure_modes.mode: A workflow agent emits findings that violate the pinned schema
failure_modes.detection: agent() schema validation on the workflow runtime rejects the output
failure_modes.recovery: Retry-on-mismatch (runtime feature); after retry exhaustion the lens is reported failed rather than merging an invalid findings file — the merge step refuses partial invalid input

failure_modes.mode: Capability probe misdetects (claims workflows available where disabled by org policy)
failure_modes.detection: Workflow launch fails immediately; review_dispatch_path trace shows the attempted path
failure_modes.recovery: Fall back to the Task-dispatch path over the same briefs (mandatory fallback is always wired); the fallback is traced with the failure reason

failure_modes.mode: Audit sweep finds findings from an n/a-routed lens (router regression)
failure_modes.detection: Post-merge diff of findings vs the routing decision in the audit run
failure_modes.recovery: Auto-file the finding as class:regression owner:router; the detector's negative fixture set is extended to reproduce the miss before the router change ships

signals: lens_route trace event extended with per-lens verdict, score, and evidence/negative_evidence (today it logs only [id, mode] — taskplane/loop.py:857-859)
review_dispatch_path trace event: {path: workflow|dispatch, reason} on every review wave
lens_engine_failed trace event + stderr warning on any applicability-engine failure (fail-open to breadth=all)
router_regression_filed trace event whenever the audit sweep auto-files an n/a-lens finding
HEADLINE coverage segment (lenses N deep · N light · N n/a (evidenced) of 26) and the coverage map with a reason per n/a on every findings dashboard
audit-run marker in findings meta (breadth=all + audit=true) so token/precision impact is measurable against the 1.3-1.5M baseline
alerts: Router regression auto-filed: any finding from an n/a-routed lens in an audit run is filed as class:regression owner:router and surfaces as a blocking finding on the review dashboard — this is the actionable alert for detector misses

Engine fail-open: lens_engine_failed + stderr warning alerts the operator that routing degraded to breadth=all and the engine needs repair (mirrors the existing hub_signal fail-safe alert at taskplane/lens.py:128-133)
Parity break: the CI Codex parity leg fails the build when dispatch-path artifacts drift from goldens

rollout.strategy: Additive and gated by data: land taskplane/lens_signals.py + route v2 behind the presence of the stage_profiles key in lenses/catalog.json (absent key = legacy routing byte-identical, existing tests prove it); land the coverage-map v2 + HEADLINE with dual-shape rendering; ship workflows/review-wave.js with capability detection so the dispatch path remains the default wherever workflows are absent/disabled (all of Codex); dogfood on the next taskPlane review with the audit sweep forced on (breadth=all) to baseline detector honesty before relying on routed reviews; then enable routed reviews with the every-5th-review audit cadence.
rollout.rollback: Remove the stage_profiles key from lenses/catalog.json (data-only) to restore legacy routing immediately, or revert the commits — route v2 is a superset that degrades to the legacy path by design, no data migration in either direction; deleting workflows/review-wave.js (or org-disabling workflows) reverts all hosts to the Task-dispatch path, which is CI-guarded byte-identical throughout.

Will be realized in lens.dispatch_briefs (taskplane/lens.py:405-480) emitting verdict/score/evidence fields additively on each brief; realization proof at review: file:line of the added fields plus the parity fixture consuming the payload on both paths

Will be realized as the parity fixtures (workflow vs dispatch byte-compare) and the CI Codex parity leg; realization proof at review: the test files and the CI job definition

lens_evidence.evidence: Approach coherence: one selected mechanism (deterministic detectors) carries all four in-scope capabilities — stage profiles bound candidates, detectors produce verdicts+evidence, the coverage map renders them, the audit sweep polices them; the workflow wave reuses the existing brief payload rather than inventing a second dispatch model. Dependency boundaries: three named contracts (stage-profiles, lens-brief, findings-v2) isolate catalog data, the router/wave handoff, and the findings shape; all proposed modules are depgraph-scannable directory nodes; depth bounded contract-only. Trade-offs: three real alternatives compared with gains/costs/revisit_when; B and C rejected on determinism/evidence grounds tied to standing rules. Failure modes: five concrete modes with detection+recovery, all failing toward more coverage, never less. Verifiable delivery: every R-0001 criterion has exactly one acceptance_map row with a concrete test-level validation, and all four R-0002 criteria are mapped in secondary_requirements; guardrail preservation (breadth=all, architecture floor, security floor, byte-identical Codex path) is itself test-pinned. Self-attested: I am the designer; no independent lens agent ran against this contract — surfaced at the approval gate per policy.
